terms.gloss: a consul, the head of a consulate
terms.comment: The medieval title of the officers who looked after merchants’ rights in foreign ports (Du Cange, in Morgan–Owens), and still the Latin for a consul, with the country or the city in the genitive or as an adjective. A Roman consul was head of the state (see consul, of ancient Rome); a modern one looks after his country’s citizens and trade in a foreign city, and ranks below an ambassador.

terms.grammar: noun phrase: sēdēs with the genitive cōnsulis

phrases.english: through the good offices of our consul at Smyrna
